articles.summary: Kanpur police arrested four for allegedly attacking devotees during a Ganesh idol immersion procession in Gujaini; several injured; attempted murder case filed, more accused sought.
articles.body: Times News NetworkKanpur: Police on Friday arrested four people for allegedly attacking devotees during a Ganesh idol immersion procession near Fattepur village in Gujaini police station area of the city on Thursday. The accused were later paraded in the area to create fear of the law among criminals.Those arrested were Shobhit Singh of Galla Mandi in Hanumant Vihar, Rahul Bhadauria of Arra village, and Dhanraj Singh Bhadauria and Jugraj Singh Bhadauria of Fattepur Dakshin.DCP (South) Deependra Nath Chaudhary said Arpit Shukla, a Galla Mandi resident, and his associates were taking a Ganesh idol for immersion in Bidhnu canal. After the procession crossed Pandu river bridge and reached Fattepur village, the accused and several associates allegedly stopped and attacked it.Ansh Sharma alias Sudama, a KDA Colony resident, was seriously injured after being struck with an axe. Aviral Dubey, Mayank and a woman were also injured and admitted to a Hospital.Police said an earlier dispute between Arpit and Shobhit Singh Rana alias Shobhit Thakur had led to the attack. An FIR over an alleged assault on Arpit had been registered at Hanumant Vihar police station. The accused allegedly pressured Arpit to withdraw the case and attacked him after he refused.Police registered a case, including charges of attempted murder and rioting, following a complaint by Ansh’s sister, Akanksha Sharma.Chaudhary denied reports of bombing or aerial firing, saying only firecrackers were burst. articles.title: Remove objectionable morphed explicit photo of woman with PM: HC to Meta
articles.summary: Delhi HC orders Meta to remove morphed explicit photo of woman with PM Modi; issues notices to 4 CJP members and directs police protection, seeks status report.
articles.body: New Delhi: Noting that the issue also involves the Prime Minister, Delhi High Court Friday ordered Meta platforms to immediately remove a woman’s morphed photograph with PM Modi from social media.It also sent a notice to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members Saurav Das, Abhijit Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh on a plea by the woman alleging that they had circulated her morphed and explicit photo with the PM.“In such matters, I would not have entertained because you have alternative remedies available, but it is not just a matter of the lady but also the Prime Minister of the country. If they are not sensitive, I will ensure they become sensitive. And I believe action will be taken,” Justice Girish Kathpalia said.While listing the matter for further hearing on Oct 14, HC directed the woman be given complete police protection after she submitted that she had been receiving threats to her life.Her lawyer said though an FIR was registered in this regard, no concrete steps had been taken to apprehend those responsible or to secure the immediate takedown or blocking of the viral deepfake links.“During recent protests held by CJP at Jantar Mantar, respondents No. 2 to 5 (the CJP members) along with their active accomplices unauthorisedly harvested the personal photograph of the petitioner and utilised AI face-swapping tools to morph her face onto a highly vulgar, compromising image alongside the PM,” the plea said.At the outset, Justice Kathpalia said the issue relating to the takedown of the objectionable content had to go to a civil court. However, he added that looking at the sensitivity involved, the woman should not be made to run from one place to another, and all the prayers will be dealt with in HC itself.“It is not just her face. Of course, she is a victim... other face (PM’s) should have also been blurred (in record),” the judge said.HC asked the woman to furnish her exact address to the investigating officer and directed police to provide her protection in all possible and practical manners.Regarding the woman’s right to compensation, the court cited the legal position that for an illegality committed during a demonstration, the victim has a right to claim compensation from the organisers of the protest, and made it clear that the pendency of this petition will not remove her right to claim any other relief to which she is entitled under law.It also directed Delhi Police to file its status report within a week, giving the exact details of the action taken in the matter and further asked the court registry to redact the victim’s name and web links from the petition and annexures.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Trump confirms he will meet with Xi two more times this year
articles.summary: President Trump on Friday confirmed he will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping two more times before the end of the year, following his counterpart’s three-day state visit to the U.S. Trump said in a TruthSocial post that he will meet with Xi in China this November for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, as…
articles.body:
President Trump on Friday confirmed he will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping two more times before the end of the year, following his counterpart’s three-day state visit to the U.S.

Trump said in a TruthSocial post that he will meet with Xi in China this November for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, as well as in December during the G20 Summit in Miami.

“President Xi and Madam Peng have just left D.C., heading for China. The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A.,” Trump wrote. “Much has been, and will be, accomplished. I look forward to our next meeting!”

Earlier on Friday, during a tea with Trump and first lady Melania Trump, Xi said he and Trump will have two more opportunities to meet this year in China and the U.S.

“We will,” Trump said, responding to Xi’s initial invitation.

Xi wrapped his second state visit to the U.S. on Friday. He last visited the country during the Obama administration in 2015.

Trump literally rolled out the red carpet for Xi despite facing criticism on both sides of the aisle over the historically adversarial relationship between Washington and Beijing.

Republican and Democratic senators cited allegations that China has aided Iran in its war against the U.S., as well as Beijing’s poor human rights record.

Trump himself criticized then-President Obama for his lavish welcome of Xi at the time.

Trump told reporters on Friday that he and Xi discussed the Iran war. U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue also said on Friday that Trump made it clear to Xi that China helping Iran is unacceptable.

The two leaders also discussed artificial intelligence during their meetings. The U.S. president also suggested there could be an agriculture deal in the works.

“I think our farmers are going to be very happy, a lot of very positive things happened,” Trump said on Friday.
